newsitem.title: USA: Archer seeks partial repeal of 2% de minimis rule.
newsitem.headline: Archer seeks partial repeal of 2% de minimis rule.

text.p: In a surprise move, the chairman of the U.S. House Ways and Means Committee, Bill Archer, called Monday for partial repeal of the "de minimis" rule on corporate holdings of tax-exempt bonds.

"The fact that the pro-rata disallowance (provision) is in there is a bit of a surprise because there has been zero support on Capitol Hill," Micah Green, executive vice president of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, said in a telephone interview.
"Chairman Archer himself has expressed opposition to doing this," Green pointed out.
Green was referring to Archer's proposal that firms with over $1 million of their assets in tax-exempt bonds no longer qualify for tax relief.
Currently, the Internal Revenue Service does not permit businesses to deduct interest on debt that they use to finance the purchase of tax-exempt bonds.

But in 1972, in what has been dubbed the de minimis rule, IRS said that it will not monitor whether a corporation has borrowed to purchase tax-exempt bonds as long as those holdings total less than two percent of a firm's net assets.
At a press conference to announce his $85 billion tax relief plan, Archer on Monday called for a reduction in allowable de minimis holdings from two percent of a firm's assets to $1 million.
Green said that the $1 million figure would "have a negative effect, but not quite as negative as the Clinton Administration's proposal."
President Clinton in February called for full repeal of the two percent de minimis rule.
"If that's where they drew the line, that's a far more acceptable proposal, albeit it's still not good," Green said, referring to Archer's $1 million figure.
